sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: Nothing; gives alternate names (Bambadion-Kheso, Kheso), population 1,300 (1983 SIL), villages, and lexical similarity 56% Dogoso, 14% Dogosé, 13% Khisa; no typology line.

sources.citation: Miehe, Gudrun, Klaus Schneider & Kerstin Winkelmann. 1993. Les forgerons dans le sud-ouest du Burkina Faso: rapports pour une comparaison entre les données ethnologiques et linguistiques. Berichte des Sonderforschungsbereichs 268, Bd. 1: 79-87. Frankfurt a. M. (urn:nbn:de:hebis:30-35851)
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: Nothing. Blacksmith-vocabulary comparison across SW Burkina languages; Khe is only named as a member of the Dogose-Gan subgroup ('kà, kpatOgO, dOgO, khi et khe', p. 83) and in a few lexical comparisons; no remarks on tone or accent.

sources.citation: Winkelmann, Kerstin. 2007. C1. Khe. In G. Miehe & K. Winkelmann (eds.), Noun Class Systems in Gur Languages, Vol. I: Southwestern Gur Languages (without Gurunsi) (Gur Monographs 9), 181-193. Köln: Rüdiger Köppe. ISBN 978-3-89645-119-4.
sources.tag: likely states stress; not yet obtained
sources.access_detail: print only (no digital copy found when the work was looked up)
sources.note: The only modern description of Khe by the sole fieldworker on the language; the parallel chapters in the same volume open with 'phonological remarks' stating tones and stress (Kaasa pp. 111-112, Khisa p. 147 'stress on the first syllable in disyllabic words'), so pp. 181-182 are the most likely place for any statement on Khe tone/stress.

sources.citation: Winkelmann, Kerstin. 2007. C2. Dogosu (pp. ca. 194-208) and C3. Khe-Dogosu: Comparative notes (pp. 209-210). In Miehe & Winkelmann (eds.), Noun Class Systems in Gur Languages I (Gur Monographs 9). Köln: Köppe.
sources.tag: likely states stress; not yet obtained
sources.access_detail: print only (no digital copy found when the work was looked up)
sources.note: Dogosu (= Dogoso [dgs]) is Khe's closest relative (56% lexical similarity per Ethnologue); Winkelmann's phonological remarks for the pair may be stated once for both or cross-referenced ('as in Khe').

sources.citation: Miehe, Gudrun, Ulrich Kleinewillinghöfer, Manfred von Roncador & Kerstin Winkelmann. 2007. Part I: Overview on noun classes in Gur (pp. 7-100), and Miehe's B-group chapters (Kaasa pp. 102-127, Khisa pp. 146-159) in the same volume.

sources.note: Group-level remarks on stress in the Kaansa-Dogose-Khisa-Khe cluster (first-syllable stress triggering C2 strengthening; penultimate stress strengthening suffix nasals) that a reader of the Khe chapter would need for context; same physical volume as item 1.
